Title: Investigations of instability mechanisms of buoyant flow in a vertical porous layer
Abstract: The present work aims to investigate the stability of buoyant flow in a vertical layer of fluidsaturated newlineporous medium by employing Darcy and non-Darcy models under the regimes of newlinelocal thermal equilibrium and nonequilibrium. In the investigation, several issues have been newlinetackled, in particular, volumetric internal heating, viscosity variation with temperature, solute newlineconcentration field, and maximum density. A combination of analytical and numerical newlinemethods such as the Chebyshev collocation method and/or the Galerkin method is employed newlineto examine a wide range of physical parameters, yielding significant insights on the stability newlinecharacteristics of the system. To address this, the probe incorporates linear stability theory, newlinewhich allows for the determination of criteria for the onset of stationary and/or travellingwave newlinemode instability. The intricate interaction between a uniform volumetric heat source newlineand the Prandtl-Darcy number has revealed the possibility of inducing instability in the base newlineflow. The influence of linear temperature-dependent viscosity on the stability of the system is newlinediscussed and established that the base flow remains stable for all infinitesimal disturbances. newlineThe study of solute concentration field on the Gill-Rees problem has explored some novel newlinefindings not found hitherto in the studies of double-diffusive convection in a vertical porous newlinelayer under the local thermal equilibrium regime and also in non-porous layers. Later, the newlineimplementation of the Brinkman porous medium with quadratic density law on the stability of newlinebase flow is examined. Lastly, potential future research directions related to the problems newlineaddressed in this thesis are discussed. newline

Title: Preparation of Chalcogenide Based Nanocomposites for Photocatalytic and Electrocatalytic Applications
Abstract: The presented thesis titled quotPreparation of Chalcogenide Based Nanocomposites for Photocatalytic and Electrocatalytic Applicationsquot is focused on the synthesis of chalcogenide-based materials and newlinetheir composites using a hydrothermal approach. The synthesis procedures were carefully optimized and doping was performed to enhance the overall catalytic activity of the chalcogenides. Furthermore, the grafting of chalcogenide materials with carbon-based materials was demonstrated to increase their overall efficiency, particularly in photocatalytic degradation and electrocatalytic newlinewater splitting applications. A variety of analytical and spectroscopic techniques, including PXRD, XPS, DRS, TGA, BET, FESEM and HRTEM, were utilized to confirm the successful synthesis of these chalcogenide materials and their composites. Specifically, the use of alkali metal chalcogenide (NaFeS2) for electrocatalytic water splitting applications demonstrated superior newlineperformance in both HER and OER compared to FeS2 alone, highlighting the noteworthy improvement in catalytic activity achieved through the introduction of alkali metal onto the FeS2 system. Similar positive results were obtained when doping Bismuth sulphide with Na, indicating a notable improvement in the photocatalytic activity of NaBiS2, leading to the successful removal newlineof 2,4-DCP. To further improve the efficiency of metal chalcogenides, CoSe2 was successfully grafted onto gC3N4 using a hydrothermal approach. The resulting composite material exhibited superior catalytic activity in both the photocatalytic removal of bisphenol A and electrocatalytic water splitting compared to the bare material, highlighting the significant improvement achieved newlinethrough grafting. Additionally, the successful doping of alkali metal onto NiS nanomaterial resulted in enhanced degradation of 2,4-DCP and improved activity in both HER and OER processes. This doping involved the introduction of S onto gC3N4, which was further grafted with NiSe2 nanomaterial to elucidate their catalytic effect.

Title: Effects of Quantum Entanglement and Decoherence on the Dynamics of Nash Equilibria in Quantum Games
Abstract: This thesis undertakes an exploration into the interplay of quantum entanglement and quantum noise, specifically focusing on their cumulative effects in driving Nash equilibria within quantum games. Investigating various noise channels such as amplitude damping, depolarising, and phase damping, the study delves into the dynamic nature of Nash equilibria and examines the potential for abrupt transitions akin to entanglement thresholds. A central objective is to construct comprehensive Entanglement-Decoherence-Nash-Equilibria diagrams analogous to phase diagrams in physics, highlighting how slight parameter variations can lead to significant shifts in system behavior. Furthermore, the research endeavors to analyze the influence of both Markovian and non-Markovian quantum noise on quantum game dynamics, employing Kraus operators within the Eisert-Wilkens-Lewenstein (EWL) protocol. Various noise models, including Random Telegraphic Noise, Modified Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Noise, and Power Law Noise, are integrated into quantum circuits before and after player strategy application. Utilizing an algorithmic quantum circuit model, the study scrutinizes player payoffs and Nash equilibria transitions across different regimes, particularly examining the behavior of transition thresholds as the entanglement parameter varies. Additionally, the thesis introduces a quantum adaptation of the two-player traveler s dilemma game, which poses unique challenges in maintaining the game s integrity and complexity while transitioning from classical to quantum realms. Contrary to classical analysis predicting descent to a Nash equilibrium with the worst payoff via backward induction, experiments suggest individuals and groups opt for strategies yielding significantly higher payoffs, thus warranting a quantum perspective on this intriguing game scenario. newline

Abstract: In vitro Plasma protein binding (PPB) and metabolic stability of three different classes of drugs were investigated in plasma and liver microsomes of dog, minipig, monkey and human to find out the best non-rodent pre-clinical species out of dog, minipig and monkey. Nine marketed non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs, namely, celecoxib, diclofenac, flurbiprofen, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, meloxicam, naproxen and piroxicam), eleven marketed cardiovascular drugs (CV drugs namely, amiodarone, atenolol, digoxin, diltiazem, labetalol, metoprolol, nifedipine, propranolol, newlinequinidine, verapamil and warfarin) and two new chemical entities (NCEs, antituberculosis drugs, namely B3 and B16) were investigated. The plasma protein binding study was conducted by most popular, reliable equilibrium dialysis method and HT Dialysis apparatus. The pH adjusted plasma from different species dog, minipig, monkey and human were spiked with test compounds and newlinekept at incubator shaker at 37 °C, 60 rpm and 5% carbon dioxide atmosphere for 6 hours to check the plasma protein binding and stability of the test compounds in plasma. Title: Cytotoxic and antitumor activities of Manilkara kauki and manilkara hexandra
Abstract: The present study explores the cytotoxic and antitumor potential of ethanolic leaf extract of Manilkara kauki (EEMK) and Manilkara hexandra (EELMH) through comprehensive in vitro, in vivo, and in silico investigations. Successive ethanolic extraction of both species yielded bioactive phytoconstituents alkaloids, glycosides, phenolic compounds, flavonoids, triterpenoids, and saponins known for their antioxidant and anticancer properties. Quantitative phytochemical analysis confirmed a higher phenolic (46.35 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid (511.6 mg QAE/g) content in M. kauki compared to M. hexandra. newlineIn vitro cytotoxicity studies using MTT assay, Trypan Blue exclusion, and DAPI staining demonstrated concentration dependent effects in both extracts, with M. kauki showing greater potency (ICand#8325;and#8320; and#8776; 265 and#956;g/ml) than M. hexandra (ICand#8325;and#8320; and#8776; 612 and#956;g/ml). Apoptotic features were confirmed by nuclear condensation and fragmentation in treated EAC cells. In vivo evaluations in EAC-bearing Swiss albino mice revealed significant tumor regression, improved survival time, and restoration of hematological and biochemical parameters upon treatment with both extracts.
